ThingDef.label: Helghan Tactical Helmet
ThingDef.description: The iconic symbol of the Helghan armed forces, and the bare minimum for any soldier committed to their cause, the tac helmet and gasmask are considered formidable urb and midworld tech for a mass production line infantryman's gear. Assembled quickly and neatly with composite plates, the tac helmet is designed to absorb sharpnel and small arms calibers. Ear pieces aid the unit in dampening loud noises at minimal cost to situational awareness. Coupled with the baleful eyes of the iconic helghan gas mask, this symbol- the unremiting gaze of a faceless soldier- has become someting of a propaganda darling for the regime. The combination is known to negatively impact social relations- even among other helghast, who have a hard time reading expressions whilst wearing this kit.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Mark 1-X Raider Helmet
ThingDef.description: An attempt largely by the Visari Corporation to create alternative infantry armor to break into Stahl dominated markets and find more affordable alternatives to their costly powered armor program, the Raider helmet is part of a cohesive 'Ultralight Assault' suit intended to be proposed as a full on replacement to conventional infantry gear. It was unveiled just months before the siege of Helghan itself, meaning production was rushed and several features cut. The basic idea was to make a helmet that was lighter but still provided something close to the defensive ability of a normal tac helm. In this they somewhat succeeded- the unified mask and helmet is lighter and somewhat aerodynamic, theoretically cutting down on wind resistance. The mask was where most of the real defense plating resided, being a weapons grade ceramic plate composition. Other features included a pressurized oxygen capsule, low-light goggles with a four way camera, and a built in radio. Unlike conventional gasmasks, this setup can actually provide void resistance, however its light materials do not prevent freezing, meaning it would only ever be good in short spacewalks of desperation. The helmet saw wider rollout than the armor it was designed for, and was often spotted among shock infantry and light machine gunners, who took a liking to it for its low overall weight and comfort.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Cold-Weather Tac-Helm
ThingDef.description: The iconic symbol of the Helghan armed forces, and the bare minimum for any soldier committed to their cause, the tac helmet and gasmask are considered formidable urb and midworld tech for a mass production line infantryman's gear. Assembled quickly and neatly with composite plates, the tac helmet is designed to absorb sharpnel and small arms calibers. Ear pieces aid the unit in dampening loud noises at minimal cost to situational awareness. Coupled with the baleful eyes of the iconic helghan gas mask, this symbol- the unremiting gaze of a faceless soldier- has become someting of a propaganda darling for the regime. The combination is known to negatively impact social relations- even among other helghast, who have a hard time reading expressions whilst wearing this kit.\n\nThis tac-helm has been cold-weather proofed, and adorned with rudimentary whitewash stripe camouflage. The inside has been lined and padded to better retain heat, and the normally exposed areas around the neck have been sealed up for long term exposure to the elements.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Veiled Tactical Helmet
ThingDef.description: A derivative of the standard tactical helm, many regular units of the army opt to use veils to mask the outline of their gas hoses, these veils eventually became optional attachments. A modicum of effort was put towards allowing veils to mask heat signatures to help infantry hide from IR/heat sensors, but these efforts were largely considered failures. The infantry's fascination with this idea of "further masking the face" was noted for later armor designs, For the riflemen however, it merely represents a desire by its users to gain some small edge in combat. Some swear it helps them hunt and forage, working well with shooting blinds and camouflage, but this claim seems dubious and some officers ban the practice of wearing this outright.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Cold-Weather MK2 Marksman Helmet
ThingDef.description: By the end of the Battle of Pyrrhus, it became clear that hunting IRS light troops was causing a 'brain drain' among marksmen as casualties rose. More than that, the tri-optics were expensive and did a poor job of keeping troops safe. Visari Corporation offered a solution; one large 'drone optic' refitted onto a mark 2 tactical helmet. The compromise gave rise to dedicated marksmen organic to every infantry section- a practice which had occured before to some extent, but now existed on official tables of organisation and equipment. They were often assigned recon, hunting, and watch missions, It soon became standard practice to mandate at least one per patrol, thanks to the optics way of foiling enemy ambushes.\n\nThis Marksman Helmet has been cold-weather proofed, and adorned with rudimentary whitewash stripe camouflage, and a snow-camo facial hood. The inside has been lined and padded to better retain heat, and the normally exposed areas around the neck have been sealed up for long term exposure to the elements.

ThingDef.label: Quad-Ocular HGMk.2 Tactical Helmet
ThingDef.description: These helmets have gained the nickname 'Four-eyes' for obvious reasons. Meant for urban combat, these optics are intended to provide the user with a greater awareness of his surroundings. Corners were cut in development to lower production costs and prevent the need for advanced components, so much of this attempt would be said to be a failure by urbworld standards. Still, it is cheap. The veil here has been reinforced with a weighted Kevlar weave in the attempt to protect hoses and mask architecture. Grenadiers are often used as frontline sappers and combat engineers in their units, and are expected to deploy their explosives in close urban encounters. In reality, grenadiers try to keep distance, knowing full well that the so called much vaunted 'mark 2 helmet' provides little real difference in the life expectancy of helghast infantry. In truth, this headgear is sturdier than most of the Helghan armed forces equipment.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Cold-Weather Mk 1-A Utility Helmet
ThingDef.description: The Mark 1-Alpha series 'utility' helmets were originally envisioned by the Helghan corporation as workplace safety gear able to be compliant with the terms of earth imperial treaty. Following the rise of Visari and the reorganization that followed, this helmet was sidelined for the more iconic Mark 1 Tactical, Still, its original design philosphy- focusing on utility and general purpose use saw it come into its own in second line troops, specialists, and reserve units. Today its an often dismissed relic, but still enjoyed by troops like Helghan tank hunters, who appreciate the wider visors and better field of view, Helghan armored divisions have also taken to the helmet.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Cold-Weather Reinforced Utility Helmet
ThingDef.description: This Mark 1-Alpha helmet has been improved with a superior rebreather and reinforced with extra armor layers to make it more resistant. It is favored by Stahl Arms shock troops and arctic commandos, despite the extra cost in components and steel. When paired with a hardsuit and some cover, a soldier can fight for a long time without respite in a nuclear winter, the troops using this likely envisioned a long war in the north of Helghan against Terran and ISA units in a grinding battle of attrition that never really came. In the end, this armor took on a second life after the fall of the homeworld among remote cold-weather garrisons in the helghast diaspora.\n\nThis reinforced utility-helm has been cold-weather proofed, and adorned with rudimentary whitewash stripe camouflage. The inside has been lined and padded to better retain heat, and the normally exposed areas around the neck have been sealed up for long term exposure to the elements.

ThingDef.label: Quad-Ocular Helghast Mk.2 Tac Helmet- Commando
ThingDef.description: Doctrinally speaking, the Helghan military has always been a 'cult of the elite' built on ideological foundations of the superiority of the helghast over all other races. So determining actual skill between units is sometimes difficult. Helghast 'commando' forces are veteran, blooded infantry drawn from non-shock armies, granted better equipment and occasionally additional training. The real tell however was that entire Helghan platoons or companies would be granted the prestige of commando designation without any formal reorganization during the siege of Helghan- leading even many troops within the regime to begin to wonder if the status really meant anything. Nonetheless, this helmet is a derivative of the Helghan mark 2 helmet, equipped with quad-ocular optics intended to make the user lethal in close quarters. Most commando's jerry rig cheap civilian grade audio devices into the ear protection in order to play patriotic music in combat. Curiously, despite the veteran status of this force, their attrition rates often exceeded other army units simply because troops would overcommit to assaults or ignore fallback orders. This body of zealots was considered a prime recruitment pool for higher echelons of elite units in the army, meaning the commandoes best were routinely pilfered for more elite formations as manpower dwindled.

ThingDef.label: Helghan Rebreather
ThingDef.description: The iconic symbol of the Helghan struggle against their world, these masks are derived from mining gear utilized by the now-defunct Helghan Corporation. For a long time on Helghan, life or death was determined by ones access to this piece of equipment. Successive design iterations have improved its comfort for long-term usage and hostile conditions, but even today the modern masks worn differ little between civilian and military issue. Although the Helghast have physically adapted to no longer need these systems to survive on most of their home planet, they remain an essential component of the army, and a symbol of the perseverance of the people who used them. Compared to typical industrial gasmasks on the rim, this device is warmer, and more sturdy, providing limited protection to the eyes mouth and face, but other cultures are sometimes loathe to use them due to the negative associations with the Helghast people and the cold, inhumane baleful gaze it gives its bearer.

ThingDef.label: M-2356 Gunstellig Compact Rebreather
ThingDef.description: An example of modern (at the time of the second extrasolar war) civilian industrial rebreather unit, an improvement over the old model in most ways, with a superior air filtration unit and better stopping power against incoming shrapnel and blunt strikes thanks to its quality craftsmanship. The Compact created it as a design originally intended to simplify production lines, calling for a smaller breathing unit then the now nearly century-old 'classic' rebreather. Inspired civil engineers and scientists long awaited an chance to revise the old mass produced designs, resulting in this sleek product. During wartime, these masks were seen as favorable replacements for standard issue masks, but were typically found on rapidly mobilized home-defense units. Some remote colonies prefer producing these because they eschew cloth resources, but most helghast army troops prefer 'old reliable' compared to this mask. Principles in this mask were used for later rebreathers.
